facts.statement: Fake AI videos are spreading on social media in China during natural disasters.
facts.support: Powerful storms and flooding incidents have seen fake videos inundating social media platforms, including images of dead bodies and false depictions of flooding areas.

facts.statement: AI-generated content is being used to fabricate emergency response efforts.
facts.support: Fake videos include blatantly fake details of emergency response efforts, misleading the public during crises.

facts.statement: Fake videos have caused panic buying of emergency supplies.
facts.support: False information about power outages prompted residents to panic buy emergency supplies.

facts.statement: AI lowers the technical barriers for creating false information.
facts.support: AI dramatically lowers the technical barriers to producing false information, allowing individuals to generate convincing content easily.
The country has over 6,000 'AI companies,' according to state-controlled wire service Xinhua.

facts.statement: There have been arrests for creating fake disaster-related content.
facts.support: Recent weeks have seen arrests and punishment for the creation of bogus reports and video content.
